The test image shows a mango leaf with multiple small, round, raised blister-like galls scattered across the leaf surface — approximately 2–3 mm in diameter, brownish in color, with some appearing to have already fallen out leaving shot holes. This perfectly matches the **Gall_Midge** description: "Round, blister-shaped galls on mango leaves... galls are visible on both sides of the leaf; when galls fall out, they leave shot holes in the leaf tissue."

The Sooty_Mould reference shows a diffuse black coating/encrustation on leaves — completely different from the discrete raised circular galls in the test image.

This is the hallmark symptom of Gall_Midge. No black coating (Sooty_Mould), no powdery white growth (Powdery_Mildew), no angular lesions (Bacterial_Canker), and no sunken dark lesions (Anthracnose)."}
